_comment: Manual composition rules. Each rule defines a family pattern with one or more bases; each composition spec is templated with {b} substituted by the current base. The resolver (compositions.py) auto-derives per-symbol offsets by canonical sub-path matching in the source SVGs. Optionally, a part can carry a `position_from` chain — a list of [target, part] pairs — to override the auto-derived offset with a sum of offsets from earlier-resolved compositions. That keeps the left/right placement of a sub-symbol identical across every parent that includes it.
_multiples_doc: Each entry: every variant of `target_base` (across all fills+rotations) is N copies of the single glyph `single`. N is auto-detected as (target_sub_paths / single_sub_paths) — typically 2 or 3 per fill digit. The resolver finds each copy's position inside the target via canonical sub-path matching.

multiples._comment: SQUEEZE FLICK ALTERNATING fill 0 — 3 flicks + 2 squeezes (8 sub-paths)
SQUEEZE FLICK ALTERNATING fill 1 — 2 flicks + 3 squeezes (7 sub-paths)

_rotation_dedup_doc: Each entry names a `target_base` whose rotations 8..f are the horizontal mirror of rotations 0..7 (rot R+8 = M(rot R)) — a SignWriting convention where the upper-half rotation indices store the flopped glyph. The resolver emits a 1-part mirror composite for each. For a symmetric base (e.g. S308) the mirror also coincides with another stored rotation; for an asymmetric base (e.g. S309) it is a new outline. The matcher confirms the mirror fits and skips it otherwise.

rules.name: movement-paired-rotation
rules.comment: Pairs that combine a base S22a rot with the +4 rotation (180° opposite). User-specified: S23100 = S22a00 + S22a04 (MOVEMENT-WALLPLANE SINGLE STRAIGHT SMALL paired with its opposite-direction sibling). Iterates through the 8 rot variants of S231: rot=i uses S22a0i + S22a0(i+4 mod 8).

rules.name: face-direction-s308-s309
rules.comment: S308 + S309 (FACE DIRECTION POSITION NOSE UP OR DOWN [TILTING]). 3 fills × 16 rotations each. User-confirmed pattern: every fill-0 variant = S2ff00 + the corresponding fill-2 variant at the same rotation. Fill 1 entries are duplicates of fill 0 (so we only emit fill-0 compositions; fill-1 stay as their original outlines but should ideally point at fill-0).

rules.name: face-direction-s307
rules.comment: S307 family (FACE DIRECTION POSITION NOSE FORWARD TILTING). 6 fills × 2 rotations. Within rot 0: fill 0..2 = head + a specific marker (one of 3..5). Rot 1 column is the horizontal mirror of the rot 0 column.

rules.name: forehead
rules.comment: S311..S313: forehead/face marking families. The 00 variant is the head with a marker drawn at fill 1 (S{b}10). The marker is horizontally centred on the head; its vertical position is whatever the standalone glyph specifies (forehead crease near the top, asterisk near the centre).

rules.name: eyes
rules.comment: Basic eye families. Fill 4 = single eye; 3 = both = two copies of 4 (the eyes are identical copies, NOT mirror images); 0 = head + both; 1 = head + right eye; 2 = head + left eye. 3 and 1/2 reference the single eye 4 directly (twice for 3) and never a mirror M(4): a mirrored copy lands at a worse sub-pixel phase and renders thinner in a browser, whereas two references to the same 4 render identically so left/right stay balanced. Placement is symmetric about the face centre line (the single 4 is smaller than the upstream eye, so xmin-matching alone drifts it left): 0 centres the both-group on the head, and 1/2 take their eye position from 0's right/left eye (occurrence 0 = right, 1 = left) so head+right and head+left are mirror-symmetric — same approach as the eyebrow rule. S317/S318 are NOT here (they add an 'extra' under a S314 eye, own rule).

rules.name: eyes-with-extra
rules.comment: S317: a S314 eye plus an 'extra' mark drawn under it (a small chevron pair). Fills 4 and 3 are the EXTRA alone (4 = single, 3 = both) and keep their own source outlines; the eye is reused from S314 (S31440). Fills 0/1/2 layer head + extra + S314 eye: 1 = head + right (extra + eye), 2 = head + left, 0 = head + both. Two choices matter: (a) the extra is listed BEFORE the eye so the eye's bbox tolerance doesn't greedily claim one of the extra's sub-paths; (b) the eye is referenced un-mirrored (S31440), not M(S31440), for the same sub-pixel-balance reason as the basic eye rule. NB: S318 is deliberately NOT here. Its 'extra' is a single caret whose bbox is almost identical to the eye's, so the bbox matcher can't tell eye from extra (it swaps them, or groups both eyes on one side); S318 keeps its correct hand-drawn source outline instead. Composing it would need a shape-aware matcher.

rules.name: eyes-with-extra-s318
rules.comment: S318 also = a S314 eye + an 'extra' under it, but its extra is the WIDE 'W' zigzag in fill 3 ({b}30), not fill 4 (a small 'm', a different variant). Unlike S317, S318's eye (arc) and W extra are single sub-paths of near-identical bbox, so the matcher can't tell which is which — it swaps eye<->W (and which row is which in 0). The fix: reuse S314's ALREADY-COMPOSED head+eye glyphs as a rigid base (head+right=S31410, head+left=S31420, head+both=S31400). Matching that whole unit pins the head and eye(s) to their true positions, leaving only the real under-eye slot(s) for the W. So 1 = S31410 + W, 2 = S31420 + W, 0 = S31400 + W + W. A separate rule from S317 because the extra lives in a different fill and the eye must be locked as a composed unit.

rules.name: arrow-fill1-double
rules.comment: Arrow families S321/S324 (4 fills × 8 rotations): fill 1 (double arrow) = two copies of fill 2 (single arrow), per rotation — the same 'both = twice single' pattern as the eye fill 3 = twice fill 4. Fill 2's own rotations 2-7 are deduped by the rot8 family, so fill 1 inherits them through the reference. {b} is the symbol base (S321/S324); the 8 entries cover rotations 0-7.

rules.name: arrow-fill0-head
rules.comment: Arrow families S321-S326: fill 0 (face circle + double arrow) = S2ff00 (head) + fill 1 (the double arrow), horizontally centred on the face and placed at the height where the eyes sit — like the eye fill 0 = head + both. The vertical position comes from the matcher (the arrow's natural height in the source fill 0); only the x is centred. `loose_match` lets the arrow fall back to size-only matching when it's hand-drawn at a different scale inside the head (e.g. S32603) so it still composes — no per-glyph exception. Must run after arrow-fill1-double so fill 1 is resolved (center uses its composed bbox). {b} is the symbol base; the 8 entries cover rotations 0-7.

rules.name: arrow-fill1-double-hi
rules.comment: S327 only has 16 rotations (the others 8). This covers the mirror-half rotations 8-f for fill 1 = two copies of fill 2 (fill 2's rot 8-f are mirror-deduped). Same as arrow-fill1-double, upper half.

rules.name: arrow-fill0-head-hi
rules.comment: S327 mirror-half rotations 8-f for fill 0 = head + fill 1, centred like arrow-fill0-head. Must run after arrow-fill1-double-hi.

rules.name: cheeks
rules.comment: S32a/S32b/S32c cheeks. fill 3 = right cheek, fill 4 = left cheek (lens shapes, part of a smaller circle). In the source, fill 0/1/2 render a cheek by pushing the head's inner contour inward — a fill, not a separate sub-path — so the cheek can't be matched. It is placed geometrically with `edge`: the marker's rightmost (right cheek) / leftmost (left cheek) point, at its vertical centre, sits on the face's right / left edge, so the lens's tip meets the head outline and its body fills inward. 1 = head + right, 2 = head + left, 0 = head + both.

rules.name: head-plus-30
rules.comment: Partial-fit eyebrow-style families where fill 0 (head + both) decomposes cleanly as head + fill 3, but fill 3 itself is hand-drawn as a single unit (so we don't decompose 30 = 40 + M(40)). Just compose 00 = head + 30 with horizontal centring.

rules.name: head-plus-marker
rules.comment: Two-fill 'head + single marker' family. Fill 0 is the head with the marker drawn; fill 1 is the marker alone. Marker is horizontally centred on the head; vertical position is whatever the standalone glyph specifies. Covers nose (S331..S334) and mouth simple (S33b..S355).

rules.name: eyebrows
rules.comment: Six-fill 'head + symmetric paired marker' family. Fill 4 is the base (right side); 5 = the left side; 3 = both side-by-side (no head); 1 = head + right; 2 = head + left; 0 = head + both. The 1/2 positions inherit from the 30 placement so left and right stay symmetric across the family. Covers eyebrows (S30a..S310), air-blow/suck (S335..S336), mouth wrinkles double (S357, S358). NB: 5 is NOT built as a mirror M(4) — an exact mirror puts the two stems at complementary sub-pixel phases, so a browser renders one half faint (and the lopsidedness flips with zoom). Keeping 5's own hand-drawn outline (independently positioned from 4) renders both halves balanced at every size; 3 then composes 4+5 as two independent outlines.
